payload.name: Crossmodal Fluency-Based Preference
payload.fact: Visual objects presented with easier (more fluent) auditory stimuli receive higher liking ratings, demonstrating that fluency-based preference effects can operate crossmodally.

provenance.title: Sounds easy, looks nice: Crossmodal transfer of auditory processing fluency to visual object preference
provenance.quote_or_locus: We found that visual objects presented with easier (more fluent) auditory stimuli received higher liking ratings. This effect persisted when a temporal lag was introduced between the auditory/visual components, but was less reliable for static (as opposed to moving) objects. These results show that fluency-based preference effects can operate crossmodally
